synonyms: Bouteloua hirsuta subsp. pectinata (Feath.) Wipff & S.D.Jones
taxonomic_note: Current Kew POWO accepts Bouteloua pectinata as a distinct species. The Master Plant Pool source row used the older varietal name Bouteloua hirsuta var. pectinata.
look_here_first: Start with the ROBUST bunchgrass and often THREE TO FIVE relatively LONG straight or slightly curved pectinate combs near the top of a flowering culm. One mature branch may extend beyond its spikelets as a bare axis. This can overlap hairy grama; measure the complete heads, count branches on ONE culm, and inspect basal hair and distal rudimentary spikelet morphology.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas documents Bouteloua pectinata from Bell, Burnet, and Williamson counties, among additional Texas counties, and discusses its distinction from B. hirsuta.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Accepted-species treatment used for this learner; old infraspecific names retained as aliases.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: The quickest split from B. hirsuta is overall stature and inflorescence architecture: B. pectinata is typically taller/more robust with 3–5 longer branches and a shorter midsummer flowering window.

Measure the longer mostly straight comb, its hairy/reduced terminal portion and naked projecting branch axis with a millimeter scale.
Compare B. hirsuta: usually shorter/smaller and frequently fewer combs but counts overlap. Preserve uncertain species if diagnostic distal/vegetative structures are absent.

comparisons.key_distinctions: TALL GRAMA B. pectinata is usually robust with 3–5 often relatively long straight combs; B. hirsuta has pronounced branch hairs and bare 'stinger' but can overlap in branch count and rachis tip. Blue grama mostly 1–3 curved eyebrows, spikelets tending to extend to branch tip; Texas grama very short woolly/awned groups; red grama thin wiry small appressed racemes. Avoid a species diagnosis from size or branch count alone.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: TALL GRAMA: first find the rooted perennial bunch and 3–5 relatively long (25–45 mm) straight or gently curved one-sided combs on ONE flowering culm. At the far end, check for an AXIS-LIKE RUDIMENTARY SPIKELET with a hairy base and often bifid tip; do not mistake that structure for a simple naked rachis extension. Compare a measured hairy grama on the same scale before naming an ambiguous specimen.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measured_growth_form_and_inflorescence: Perennial tuft/bunchgrass on calcareous rocky ground; 3–5 one-sided branches typically 25–45 mm long (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas). Photograph the whole rooted plant and one attached culm to establish branch counts and size. Plant height alone is not decisive.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.ligule_collar: A short ciliate/hairy ligule at the true blade–sheath junction, not an auricle. The broad B. hirsuta species-complex treatment reports 0.2–0.5 mm hairs; this range is a COMPARISON REFERENCE, not independently measured for the distinct B. pectinata species. Obtain a true 1-mm-scale ligule and collar photograph; distinguish membrane/hair fringe from long marginal blade hairs.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet_glume_lemma_awn: Each comb carries numerous crowded, one-sided spikelets with a lower bisexual fertile floret and reduced distal sterile floret(s). Broad B. hirsuta complex references give spikelets ~5–6 mm, lower glumes ~1.4–3.5 mm, upper glumes ~3–6 mm, fertile lemmas ~2–4.5 mm with 1–3 short awns (central ~0.2–2.5 mm), and a reduced upper lemma with 3 awns (~2–4[6] mm). These are EXPLICITLY provisional complex-level reference ranges, NOT validated diagnostic B. pectinata measurements. Photograph and measure separate attached glumes, fertile lemma and rudimentary floret before publishing species-specific numeric ranges.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.critical_terminal_structure: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas distinguishes B. pectinata by an axis-like terminal RUDIMENTARY SPIKELET beyond the crowded spikelets, often hairy at base and visibly bifid under magnification. B. hirsuta can have a naked projecting rachis; labeling both as the same 'stinger' obscures an important separation.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: B. hirsuta (hairy grama) overlaps in branch counts and overall comb silhouette; check terminal axis-like rudiment versus naked rachis, leaf/sheath hair bases, whole-culm architecture, and voucher. B. gracilis (blue grama) generally has fewer, curved eyebrows and different distal branch behavior. B. rigidiseta (Texas grama) has much shorter (~10 mm) numerous branches. B. trifida (red grama) is slender with short appressed branches. Do not force species ID on immature, damaged or mixed culms.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.taxonomy_and_evidence_caution: Preserve accepted B. pectinata species concept, its historical B. hirsuta var./subsp. pectinata aliases, original county/native decisions, and all photo rights. FNA/other B. hirsuta aggregate dimensions are comparison context, not independently validated B. pectinata diagnostic measurements. Hybridization with B. hirsuta is documented and ambiguous plants need voucher review.
